correctness.rationale: For L=limsup_{t↓0}||T(t)||, strong continuity and uniform boundedness give 1<=L<infinity. For every c>L one can choose delta with ||T(t)||<=c for 0<=t<=delta and use t=n delta+r to obtain ||T(t)||<=c exp((log c)t/delta). An unbounded generator A has dense proper domain D(A); each right resolvent is injective with this dense nonclosed range, hence not Fredholm. Atkinson plus fixed uniform Calkin exponent m implies compactness of J_lambda^m, J_lambda=lambda R(lambda,A). These operators converge strongly to I, hence uniformly on compact subsets when their norms are uniformly bounded. The package estimates ||J_lambda||<=c lambda/(lambda-omega), yielding beta_K(X)<=c^m as lambda→∞ and then <=L^m. The norm-jump inequalities follow from ||T(t)-I||>=||T(t)||-1. No use of numerical experiments or unjustified extrapolation. Crucially, the same hypotheses admit a stronger standard estimate ||J_lambda^m||<=c(lambda/(lambda-omega))^m via m-fold Laplace convolution; this does not invalidate the weaker asserted bound but defeats originality/value.
